newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Ship carrying aid to Albania begins unloading.
newsitem.headline: Ship carrying aid to Albania begins unloading.

text.p: A ship carrying about 400 tonnes of humanitarian aid supplies from the United Nations World Food Programme began unloading in the western Albanian port of Durres on Wednesday, witnesses said.

The ship is carrying 360 tonnes of wheat flour and 36 tonnes of beans and marks the biggest food shipment to Albania since the launch of a multinational aid protection mission to the chaotic Balkan state.
The food supplies will be stored in a port warehouse, a WFP aid worker in Durres said. The WFP will meet military officials to discuss plans to begin distributing the aid.
The aid is aimed at hospitals, orphanages, homes for the handicapped and elderly and destitute families across Albania. A WFP official said distribution would probably start on Friday.

Nearly 1,200 Italian, French and Spanish soldiers belonging to the eight-nation U.N.-backed force arrived by land and sea in Albania on Tuesday at the start of a mission to protect delivery of emergency food aid and medicines to the country's poor.

Albania slid into anarchy last month after fraudulent investment schemes wiped out the saving of thousands of families. Nearly 300 people have been killed since people looted armouries deserted by soldiers and police.
